504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), are before this Court seeking relief.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners has placed on record a certified copy of the judgment passed by the learned I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Hubballi, in MC No. 465/2024, wherein the marriage of accused No. 1 with the de facto complainant has been mutually dissolved under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

entities.text: I Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Hubballi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The de facto complainant has agreed to withdraw all the allegations against the petitioners and has no objections to the quashing of the impugned proceedings.

4. Although the offences alleged are cognizable and non- compoundable, having regard to the fact that the de facto complainant has withdrawn all the allegations against the petitioners and has no objections to the quashing of the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise if the petitioners are subjected to trial.

The probability of the petitioners' conviction is remote and bleak,
given the settlement.
Therefore, the continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners would amount to an abuse of the process of law.
5. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
The impugned proceedings, CC No. 55/2022, on the file of the learned IV Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Dharwad, are hereby quashed.
